summary: Godrej Consumer Products makes everyday home and personal care items: mosquito repellents, air fresheners, soaps, body wash, hair colour, incense sticks and detergent. It sells them in India, Indonesia, Africa and other markets.
description: Godrej Consumer Products (GCPL) makes things that people buy again and again. For the home it makes mosquito repellents such as liquid vaporisers (a plug-in device that slowly releases repellent from a bottle), sprays and incense sticks, plus room fresheners and liquid detergent. For the body it makes soaps, body wash and hair colour. It runs five manufacturing clusters across nine countries. India is its largest market, and the report says 39 percent of its revenue in 2025-26 came from international businesses.
money: GCPL earns money by selling packaged goods to distributors, wholesalers, large store chains and online platforms, which pass them on to households. Its main costs are raw materials (the report names palm fatty acid distillate (PFAD), a by-product of palm oil refining, and materials linked to the price of crude oil), packaging, factories, advertising to keep its brands known, and the sales and delivery network. The shelf price a household pays is not GCPL's revenue, and revenue is not profit.
customers: Households use the products, but the buyers who pay GCPL directly are distributors, wholesalers, store chains, online and quick-delivery platforms and, in some African markets, salons. The report says online and quick delivery apps were the fastest-growing channel in India. In Indonesia, small neighbourhood shops did best.
drivers: How many packs it sells, the price of raw materials and packaging compared with its selling prices, how much it spends on advertising, and currency moves in the countries where it sells.

groups.title: Mosquito and insect control
groups.examples: Goodknight liquid vaporisers, Goodknight incense sticks (agarbatti) and sprays sold under the brand name HIT (a name, not an abbreviation).
groups.explanation: The report calls this Household Insecticides, meaning products that keep mosquitoes and other insects away. It says the Goodknight liquid vaporiser is being taken from India to Indonesia, Bangladesh and Nigeria.

groups.title: Air care
groups.examples: Aer air fresheners, including a small pouch called Aer Power Pocket, and Stella in Indonesia.
groups.explanation: Air care means products that scent a room. The report says Aer reached more households over four years and that Aer Power Pocket is being taken from India to Indonesia, Bangladesh, the Middle East and Latin America.

groups.title: Soap and body wash
groups.examples: Godrej No.1 soap and Cinthol foam body wash.
groups.explanation: The company's letter to shareholders says it began as a soap for India made from vegetable oils instead of animal fat. The report says a sandalwood-scented Cinthol foam body wash was launched this year.

groups.title: Hair colour
groups.examples: Godrej Expert hair colour in a cream, a black henna powder, and a shampoo form.
groups.explanation: The report says hair colour is one of the categories where few people yet use the product, so there is room to grow. A shampoo-style colour first sold in India has been launched in Indonesia.

groups.title: Detergent, toilet cleaner and baby wipes
groups.examples: Godrej Fab liquid detergent, Godrej Spic toilet cleaner and baby wipes in Indonesia.
groups.explanation: These are newer or smaller lines. The report says GCPL entered the toilet cleaner category in India this year, and that its Indonesian business gained market share in baby wipes.

basics.title: What is volume growth?
basics.text: The report talks about underlying volume growth. Typically this means growth in the number of packs sold, not growth that comes only from price rises.

basics.title: What are general trade and modern trade?
basics.text: General trade means small neighbourhood shops and the wholesalers that supply them. Modern trade means supermarkets and store chains. Online and quick-delivery apps are a third route.

basics.title: What does 'consolidated' mean here?
basics.text: The Board's report shows two sets of results. Consolidated means GCPL together with its subsidiaries in other countries. Standalone means the company alone. Check which one a figure uses.

basics.title: Why does the year end in March?
basics.text: GCPL's financial year ran from 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026, which the report calls FY 2025-26, like most Indian companies.

steps.title: Buy raw materials and packaging
steps.text: GCPL buys materials such as palm fatty acid distillate, rubber, paper and crude-oil-linked inputs from suppliers, and keeps stock cover for critical inputs.

steps.title: Make and pack the products
steps.text: Factories fill bottles, press soap, wrap incense sticks and pack pouches. The report says it is automating lines and cutting the number of product variants it makes.

steps.title: Sell to distributors, chains and platforms
steps.text: GCPL sells to distributors and wholesalers, who supply small shops, and to store chains and online platforms. In Indonesia it moved some direct shop deliveries to distributors.

steps.title: Advertise and support the brands
steps.text: GCPL spends on advertising and on getting products into more homes, so shoppers choose its brands from the shelf.

steps.title: Bill and collect
steps.text: Revenue (what GCPL bills), profit (what is left after costs) and cash received are different things, and each can move in a different direction in a year.

specifics.title: The same product travels between countries
specifics.text: The report says a product that works in one market is moved to others: the Goodknight vaporiser from India abroad, and Aer Matic, an air freshener first sold in Indonesia, to India. This spreads design costs over more sales.

specifics.title: Smaller packs to reach more buyers
specifics.text: The company's India website says smaller value packs such as the HIT no-gas spray, the Goodknight mini liquid vaporiser and the Godrej Expert Rich Creme let more people afford its products.

specifics.title: A large share of sales is outside India
specifics.text: The report says 39 percent of revenue came from international businesses in 2025-26. Each region has its own competitors, prices and currency, so a good year in one place can be offset by a weak year in another.

specifics.title: Part of the Godrej group, but not the whole group
specifics.text: The report says GCPL is a member of the Godrej Industries Group. The group also has other businesses; their sales and profits are not part of this company.

watch: Are higher raw material costs being passed on without losing buyers?
The report says it has been careful about passing on higher input costs. If prices rise too fast, shoppers may buy fewer packs.
Compare the growth in packs sold with the change in revenue and profit margin in each results release.
How are the international regions doing compared with India?
Indonesia, Africa and Latin America each had a different year in 2025-26, and together they make up a large share of revenue.
Read the region-by-region commentary in the Board's report and compare it with the previous year.
Is selling online and by quick delivery growing faster, and what does it cost?
The report says these channels are the fastest growing in India, but they can carry different margins from small shops.
Read the channel commentary and the notes on selling and distribution costs over several years.
The letter to shareholders calls the liquid vaporiser category an unsolved problem, because share and use have not risen as much as hoped.
Look for the company's later comments on this category and on how many homes use vaporisers.
How much do currency swings cost?
A large share of sales is in other currencies, and the report names currency movements as a risk.
Read the notes on foreign exchange and hedging and compare reported results with results at constant currency if given.
risks: The report says prices of PFAD and crude-linked materials rose sharply in the last quarter of the year. If GCPL cannot raise selling prices in step, profit per pack falls.
The report says unfavourable currency moves and open exposures could put pressure on cash flow and profit, and that a forex committee monitors them every month.
The report notes that stricter rules or bans on some ingredients or packaging materials such as plastic could force GCPL to change products or packs.
The report names rising transport costs, container shortages and longer lead times as threats to product availability in shops.
context: January to March 2026: input prices jumped after the West Asia crisis

The report says prices of PFAD and crude-linked materials surged in the last quarter of 2025-26 (January to March 2026) because of the West Asia crisis. It says GCPL held stock of critical inputs, looked for other suppliers, and has been prudent in passing increased costs on to consumers.

financialNotes.title: How to read the figures
financialNotes.text: These are consolidated figures, meaning Godrej Consumer Products and its subsidiaries together, for the year to 31 March 2026. The segments are regions, not products, so profit by brand is not disclosed. Segment result is a region's profit before depreciation, interest, one-off items and tax, so it is not profit after tax. Profit after tax is after exceptional items, costs shown separately because they are one-off, of ₹233 crore in total. Most is severance pay for restructuring, legal costs and settlements (including a US lawsuit over hair relaxer products) and extra retirement-pay provisions from India's new Labour Codes. The company also restated last year's revenue to deduct amounts owed to customers, with no change in profit. No customer is above a tenth of revenue.

stepsTitle: From a factory to a shop shelf.

quick.title: What it does
quick.text: It makes mosquito repellents, air fresheners, soaps, body wash, hair colour, incense sticks and detergent and sells them in India and many other countries.

quick.title: Who pays
quick.text: Distributors, wholesalers, store chains and online platforms buy from it. Households are the final users.

quick.title: How it earns
quick.text: It sells branded goods in packs priced for everyday buyers, including small packs, and earns more when it sells more packs of each brand.

quick.title: What it spends on
quick.text: Raw materials, packaging, factories, advertising for its brands, and the sales and delivery network.

helps.title: Many homes do not yet use these products
helps.text: The report says insecticides, air care and hair colour are still used by relatively few households in its markets, which leaves room to grow by reaching more homes rather than only by raising prices.

helps.title: Well-known brands in several countries
helps.text: The report says it holds the number one position with 12 brands across four regional clusters. Known brands help it win shelf space and repeat purchases.

helps.title: Savings used to pay for brand building
helps.text: The report's strategy is to fund more spending on brands through simplification: more factory automation and fewer product variants, so each product sells in larger volumes.

hurts.title: Competition can squeeze profit
hurts.text: The report says Indonesia faced heightened competitive intensity in household insecticides. Packs sold there rose, but the Indonesian business's sales and operating profit fell slightly.

hurts.title: Some markets are harder than others
hurts.text: The report says South Africa's Hair Fashion business and Ghana's external market volatility needed continued attention, and that dollar-channel distribution and Middle East pricing held back US sales.

hurts.title: Advertising has to keep rising
hurts.text: The report says Africa's profit margin absorbed higher above-the-line investments, meaning advertising and brand spending. Holding a brand's place on the shelf can reduce short-term profit.
